subject: Proposal: queue jitter mitigation + reservation credit framework for dedicated pool
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nimbus-analytics.com>, Nimbus Analytics Procurement <procurement@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: queue jitter mitigation + reservation credit framework for dedicated pool

Hi Olivia / Procurement team,

Quick note following our demo last week — thanks again for the time. Nimbus's production traffic showed a few short windows of "queue jitter" when burst demand and nightly batch jobs coincided; I wanted to propose a simple addendum we think will keep your latency SLOs steady without over-committing capacity.

High-level proposal:
- Contract-level guarantee: preserve the Dedicated pool throughput at 95% of provisioned sustained throughput for 99.9% of 1-minute intervals each month (we can work on exact wording).
- Remediation: where throughput falls below the threshold for >10 consecutive minutes due to queueing/eviction behavior, Redwood issues reservation credits that offset part of the monthly Dedicated spend.
- Operational controls: prioritized lanes for interactive traffic + a small pre-warm window around your nightly batch jobs.

I've attached a short calculation workbook (headroom_calc.xlsx) showing how credits would be computed for a sample month and a draft SLO blurb (sample_slo_text.txt) you can share with legal.

Are you available for a 30-min call on Wed to review mechanics and acceptable credit sizing? If you prefer, we can surface a redline for your procurement team first.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Sales - Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0172

Attachments: headroom_calc.xlsx, sample_slo_text.txt

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T14:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: queue jitter mitigation + reservation credit framework for dedicated pool

Hi Ben,

Thanks — this looks promising. A couple of clarifying asks before we loop legal:

1) Define “queue jitter” and the detection window: is this measured at request enqueue time, server-side queue depth, or per-pool throughput? Nimbus needs a precise metric to avoid disputes.
2) Can you provide historical headroom numbers for the last 90 days on a similarly-sized pool? That will help us estimate expected credits.
3) What’s your proposed cap on monthly credits (we can’t have unlimited downside).

Procurement: please confirm what contract doc you want redlined (MSA or dedicated addendum).

If we can get numbers today, we can discuss on Thursday.

—Olivia
Olivia Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Nimbus Analytics
olivia.park@nimbus-analytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: queue jitter mitigation + reservation credit framework for dedicated pool

Thanks for the quick read, Olivia. Short answers and attachments below.

1) Definition / detection
- We measure detection at the per-pool egress throughput level (tokens/sec) aggregated into 1-minute buckets, and we correlate with queue depth spikes and KV cache miss rates. For the addendum we can use a formally defined metric: "sustained throughput below X tokens/sec for N consecutive 1-minute buckets."

2) Historical numbers
- Attached workbook (headroom_calc.xlsx) has a 90-day sample from a 24-GPU pool we run for a customer with similar patterns. See tabs: "raw_samples" and "credit_examples."

3) Credit cap
- Suggested safety cap: credits up to 10% of monthly reserved spend for a single pool; aggregate cap 20% across linked pools. Credits computed pro-rata using the formula in the workbook.

Operational controls (how we prevent recurrence)
- Priority lane for interactive traffic (soft preemption for batch jobs).
- 10-minute pre-warm window we trigger before scheduled nightly batches (we can use your job schedule or a webhook).
- Optional: a sticky reservation setting that favors long-lived KV caches for your session traffic.

Next step: Marissa (cc) can walk through the runbook and propose the exact SLO language to give to your contracts team. If Procurement prefers, we’ll produce a redline addendum that implements the caps above.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Sales - Redwood Inference

Attachments: headroom_calc.xlsx, sample_slo_text.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nimbus-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: queue jitter mitigation + reservation credit framework for dedicated pool

Hi Olivia — I ran a quick operations playbook sketch and included steps you can test in a staging window. High level (attached as queue_runbook.md):

- Observability: create a dashboard with 1-min throughput, queue depth, KV cache miss rate; alert when throughput < threshold for 2 consecutive buckets.
- Mitigation sequence (automated):
  1) Activate priority lane for interactive traffic (0–5s rule to route to reserved fast-path).
  2) If sustained >10 minutes, trigger partial preemption of batch workers and spin up a small standby pre-warm (if burst capacity allowed).
  3) If still degraded at 30 minutes, issue reservation credit and open incident.
- Test plan: schedule controlled nightly job overlap in staging for 3 nights; capture telemetry and run credit calc.

We can also instrument a webhook from Nimbus job scheduler so Redwood pre-warms automatically. Happy to run the staging tests with your ops team next week.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: queue_runbook.md

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Nimbus Analytics Procurement <procurement@nimbus-analytics.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T16:09:00-04:00
Subject: Dedicated pool SLA addendum — initial redline and credit mechanics

Hi Olivia / Procurement,

Attached is a first-pass redline (SLA_amendment_redline.pdf) implementing the operational definitions Ben and Marissa outlined. Key commercial points we propose: 

- Credit calculation: 0.5% of monthly reserved spend per 10 minutes of sustained degraded throughput after the 10-minute detection window, up to a pool-level cap of 10% of that pool's monthly reserved spend. Aggregate account cap 20% per month.
- Detection metric: per-pool sustained throughput below agreed threshold for >10 consecutive 1-minute buckets; thresholds defined per pool in Annex A.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows and customer-triggered concurrency spikes beyond a pre-declared job schedule.

If this fits your expectations we’ll: (a) incorporate any procurement edits, (b) convert to DocuSign and (c) include the runbook as an operational annex.

Please advise redline comments in the PDF; we can iterate quickly.

Regards,
David Kim
Director, Contracts — Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com

Attachments: SLA_amendment_redline.pdf

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T17:13:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool SLA addendum — initial redline and credit mechanics

David / team — thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement and I reviewed the redline this afternoon. High level: the credit formula and caps look reasonable, and the detection metric is actionable for our SREs. A few follow-ups before signature:

- Can Redwood commit to providing the 90-day telemetry export as part of the annex? We want the historical baseline attached to the contract.
- Please carve in an explicit scheduled-maintenance calendar and the webhook pre-warm integration (we can provide API keys).

If you can add those two items to the redline, Procurement will accept the addendum and we’ll proceed to DocuSign (HS record: HS-29384). Olivia will confirm final signers after the redline update.

Appreciate the pragmatic approach — happy to run the staging test next Wednesday once the pre-warm hook is in place.

—Olivia
Olivia Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Nimbus Analytics
